sections.title: Letter erre sound
paragraphs: The letter name is (erre) /ɛʁ/. It makes one main sound, heard in (rue) /ʁy/, which means street. This letter has one sound, but it can also stay quiet.

sections.title: Pronouncing erre
paragraphs: Raise the back of your tongue toward the back of the mouth. Narrow the gap so the air rubs through. Touch your throat with your hand to feel the voice buzz. For the second variant, keep the mouth still and make no sound.

sections.title: Spelling rules for erre
paragraphs: In most words, you pronounce the sound as in (rare) /ʁaʁ/. At the end of many words, it is a silent letter, like in (parler) /paʁ.le/. A silent letter is a letter that you write but do not say.

sections.title: Avoiding mistakes with erre
paragraphs: Do not curl your tongue tip back like in the English word red. Keep your tongue tip low behind your bottom teeth. Make the friction only at the very back of your throat.
